### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via timeDimensions (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection), timeDimensions (literal, a string literal in assertDeclaredMembers; a string literal in param; a string literal in undeclaredSelectionMembers))_

- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via compareTo (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection))_

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via timeDimensions (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection), timeDimensions (literal, a string literal in assertDeclaredMembers; a string literal in param; a string literal in undeclaredSelectionMembers))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class), timeDimensions (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection), timeDimensions (literal, a string literal in assertDeclaredMembers; a string literal in param; a string literal in undeclaredSelectionMembers))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class), compareTo (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection), timeDimensions (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection), timeDimensions (literal, a string literal in assertDeclaredMembers; a string literal in param; a string literal in undeclaredSelectionMembers))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via compareTo (symbol, a field of type JudgedSelection))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d67bf20ab83974be8bdfda383cbf75963d4a6beb` — the merge of head `75e3e0618cb94a53f65b32ab6a9eaef7374a1659` into base `951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d67bf20ab83974be8bdfda383cbf75963d4a6beb && git checkout d67bf20ab83974be8bdfda383cbf75963d4a6beb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f 75e3e0618cb94a53f65b32ab6a9eaef7374a1659 && git checkout -B drift-repro 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f && git merge --no-ff 75e3e0618cb94a53f65b32ab6a9eaef7374a1659

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `73cf3b1ff7be20c5962d743ec82ad4054c57ad5f`
Area: S2 / A3 · Fixes #34005 · L1, the ordinary ACCEPT read per review-checklist.md. The narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, maintainer ruling 6902027136, questions ruled A in 6904231154) also owes L2 its CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record. This PASS does not stand in for that record.

1. **One rule, lifted rather than forked.** `undeclaredSelectionMembers` (`dataset-declared-members.ts`) is the old `assertDeclaredMembers` body moved out, line for line, with the same `(member, param)` dedupe and the same three positions (`measures`, `dimensions`, `timeDimensions[].dimension`). The AI face now calls it and keeps its own wording, including the 非指标口径 fallback. The second ablation leg (7 red in `dataset-tools.test.ts`) shows the tool still judges before anything is read.
2. **Where the door refuses, and in what order.** `assertSelectionMembersDeclared` runs in `answerDataset` after `compile` and before the draft-preview branch and any read.
   - A missing dataset is still answered 404 first.
   - A caller the catalogue admission does not admit is answered by the read gate (`assertQueryObjectsExposed`, then `assertReadAdmitted`), so they never see a member list. If that gate passes anyway, the throw gets `undefined` admission and lists `(none)`. The refusal never names a withheld or `internal` member (ADR-0100).
   - The admission is asked only on the refusal path, so the served path costs nothing new.
   - It judges against every declared member, so a declared member the caller may not read still reaches the 403 field gate. The CONTROL pins this.
3. **The dataset-door remedy (`5a127a4cc9`).** `datasetDoor: compiled !== undefined` is set only on a `queryDataset` call's scope, and the draft preview passes `true`. Each `ensureCube` path (inferred, augmented, declared) forwards it to both source-field gates. The cube door's sentence is byte-identical. I checked the one dogfood file that asserts the cube hint (`analytics-adhoc-query-isolation`): it reads `/analytics/query` and `/analytics/sql` only, so it is unaffected. The flag ablation turns 3 red and leaves the cube-door control green.
4. **Tests.** The new service file and the new dogfood file assert `code` and `status` on every refusal. The in-process cases also assert `member`, `param`, `cube`, the usable list, the remedy and that nothing was read. The batch door refuses one entry and serves its declared sibling. The re-targeted pins were judged one by one and none was loosened. The removed backed-join CONTROLs passed only through a minted raw path, and `preview-time-filter-fk-parity` now declares the FK dimensions it selects. The four rest pins reach their original gates through a stale declared member, and the relationship-path case is correctly re-read as a 400 before any read.
5. **Wire shape is consistent.** The REST body is `{ code, message }`, and the changeset, `analytics.mdx` and the body all say so now. `data-api.mdx` limits the inferred spellings to the cube query.
6. **Declarations.**
   - The title carries `!`, and the changeset carries the BREAKING banner with the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker.
   - `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing in `packages/spec` moves, and this is a runtime refusal.
   - The `Skills-docs:` line is present and holds.
   - The census (H2) found 0 hits across app-crm, showcase, platform-objects and hotcrm at `e7490b6`, with a 6-hit positive control.
7. **Dogfood battery.** The full battery ran at `b263c8df14` (470 passed, 3 skipped of 473 files). It is not pinned to this head, because `5a127a4cc9` and the rest pins came after it. I accept that under the binding 16:10Z cost rule (area-rules.md): service-analytics is not one of the shared packages that need a local battery, and the merge group runs the Dogfood shards on the queued tree. The PR's `Dogfood Regression Gate` is success.
8. **Merge and checks.** `73cf3b1f` is a clean merge of main into `e2a0a9c2`. The own-diff patch-id is `bcabd56b41` on both, so the merge brought only main's changes. Check-runs on the head: 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed or pending. `mergeable_state` is clean, and `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` `babda9d339` is clean.
9. **Noted, not owed.** The preview path's member-minting branch in `answerDataset` is now unreachable for selection members. The body records this as an observation only. A later cleanup can delete it.

The patch-id is `bcabd56b41c72cd049d95be8ee846c99d2b3f194`. A clean main merge that keeps it keeps this PASS.

Read at 2026-11-16T05:15Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6907821382; no lane request (owed per check-owed-reviews). Independence: implemented in a project thread for domain:server#5 (zhuangjianguo); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

No prior contract-review record exists for this PR, so no finding id is continued. The lane PASS 6906476633 is not adopted; every conclusion below was re-derived from the diff.

### ① Derived judgments

Judged against card #34005, the maintainer ruling recorded in 6902027136 and the four seat rulings in 6904231154.

- **The ruling's rule is implemented, at one point every entry passes.** `answerDataset` calls `assertSelectionMembersDeclared` after the dataset compiles and before the draft-preview branch and any read. `queryDataset` is the only caller of `answerDataset`. I enumerated the callers of `queryDataset` at this head: the REST single door, each entry of the batch door (both through `answerDatasetQuery` in `analytics-routes.ts`), the AI tool (`dataset-tools.ts`, which judges first with the same function and then calls the service), the two MCP bridges (through the tool), and the publish-time build probes. None reaches the executor another way.
- **The judgment is lifted, not forked.** `undeclaredSelectionMembers` is the #33958 body moved into `dataset-declared-members.ts`; the tool's `assertDeclaredMembers` now calls it and keeps its own wording.
- **Every selection key that names a member is bounded.** `measures`, `dimensions` and `timeDimensions[].dimension` are judged by exact name against the dataset's own declaration. I read the other three keys that name a member in `dataset-executor.ts`: `order` keys are held to the selected members and their compare columns, each `totals.groupings` entry to the selected dimensions, and `compareTo.dimension` to a selected time dimension that carries a window. `runtimeFilter` keys are fields, not members, and are unchanged, as the changeset says.
- **Order of answers holds as declared.** A missing dataset is 404 at the REST door before the service is asked. A caller the read gate does not admit is answered by that gate, with no member list. A declared member the caller may not read still reaches the field gate. The list of usable members comes from the caller's own admission.
- **Inline dataset (seat ruling 1, option A): upheld.** The body is its own declaration and is judged against itself; the object and field gates that bound an inline body are untouched.
- **ADR-0087 disposition (seat ruling 2, option A): upheld on shape, not on its stated reason.** No key, value or stored row changes shape, so there is nothing for a migration to rewrite. The marker's sentence that authored and save-gated dashboards already bind only declared members is not true of one class; see M2.
- **Stored-item report (seat ruling 3, option A): upheld**, subject to M2.
- **Compare window (seat ruling 4, option A): the basis does not hold.** See M2.
- **Census.** Authored stacks: 0 hits, with a positive control. I spot-checked the compare widgets in hotcrm's four dashboards against their datasets and found the same: each date-range field is also a declared date dimension of the same name. List-view and page charts are a selection site too; `chart-measure-unknown` and `chart-dimension-unknown` judge them, so the save-gate argument covers them.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-analytics`, title with `!`, BREAKING banner in the PR body and the changeset, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both, `Metadata-protocol: none`. That is the repository's form for a breaking runtime narrowing (`check-changeset-no-major` is green), and nothing in `packages/spec` moves. The level is right.

CI at this head: 53 check-runs, 38 success, 15 skipped, none failed, none pending. Nothing is still running. The pull request is still a draft.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **File surface.** Four existing `packages/rest/src/*.test.ts` pins are outside the claim's file surface (6902377406). The PR body and the request comment explain each one; they are re-targets of pins the rule made unreachable, none loosened. Flagged, not graded.
- **Governed text owed elsewhere.** The code cites ADR-0149 D1 for the closed-member rule, and the card says the ADR carries no line for it yet. The skills-lane line is "noted, not filed" in the dev report. It needs a card number before this lands, so the citation does not point at text that is not there.
- **M1's spec half is outside the claimed surface.** See M1 for the two ways to close it.
- **Cube door.** `POST /analytics/query` is outside the rule by the card. I did not review it.
- **Security discipline.** This record states rules only.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: `DatasetSelectionSchema` says the selection carries "Dimension names from the dataset" and "Measure names from the dataset", and ADR-0021 calls the dataset a closed surface. On that text the change makes the spec's own sentence real. Two things stand against a PASS.

M1 (must-fix) — Two published statements still declare the capability this PR removes, and the PR leaves both standing. `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx` (the paragraph after "Declaring a dimension confers no filterability") says the analytics query API "does accept an object's own field as an ad-hoc dimension without the dataset declaring it", and the TSDoc on the dashboard global filter's `field` in `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` says the same in almost the same words. After this change a dataset query refuses exactly that. The card's premise reading ("No ⛔ line allows undeclared members") missed both, and the docs-drift check cannot see them because they share no identifier with the diff. The maintainer's ruling still decides the behaviour; what is owed is that the published text agrees with it. Fix: correct the `dashboards.mdx` paragraph in this PR (it is inside the claimed `content/docs/**` surface). For the spec TSDoc, either widen the claim and correct it here with the spec's generated-artifact gates run, or file the card for it and cite the number in the PR body. New finding.

M2 (must-fix) — Seat ruling 4 rests on a rule that does not judge dashboards, and the breaking notice omits the consumer it affects. The ruling keeps a compare window over an undeclared date key refused because `report-date-range-dimension-unknown` "already requires declared names at save". That rule judges a report's `dateRange.dimension`. A dashboard's date range names a FIELD: the spec says `dateRange.field` (default `created_at`) resolves against the object, "not against that dataset's declared `dimensions`", and `dashboard-filter-field-unknown` enforces it against the object. No lint rule reads `compareTo` on a widget, and the publish probe asks each widget's measures with no window. By the PR's own account a compare widget lowers that date key into `timeDimensions`, and the executor's refusal text names the dashboard date-range filter as the usual source of that window. So a dashboard that passes every save and publish gate, has a compare widget, and whose date field is not also the NAME of a declared dimension, rendered before this change and is refused after it. The authored census found none because the shipped stacks name the dimension after the field; a runtime-saved or third-party dashboard has no such guarantee and no gate. The maintainer's ruling asked that no shipped dashboard break, and the changeset's breaking paragraph and ADR-0087 marker both say stored dashboards are save-gated to declared members. I could not read the renderer, which is outside this repository, so the lowering is taken from the PR body and the executor's message. Fix, all in this PR's surface except the last: (a) the seat re-rules question 4 on the true basis, or takes it to the maintainer, since it bears on the ruling's own condition; (b) the changeset's breaking paragraph and the ADR-0087 marker name this class and its remedy (declare a date dimension named as the date-range field, or set `compareTo.dimension` to a declared one, whichever the re-ruling settles); (c) the dashboards page says what a compare widget's date key must be; (d) a card for the missing save gate, cited in the PR body. The code may well stay as it is. New finding.

S1 (should-fix) — The refusal's order against the read gate is pinned for one verdict only. `dataset-query-declared-members.test.ts` pins that a caller the read gate denies gets that gate's answer and no member list, in process. There is no pin for the verdict the gate cannot reach (the 503 answer), and none over REST for either. The rule the changeset states is "never a member list"; pin it for both verdicts, and once through the REST door. New finding.

N1 (nit) — `analytics-service.ts` still carries the draft-preview comments that describe an undeclared measure and dimension being minted and judged there (#28172, #28201). That branch is now unreachable for selection members, as the PR body records. The comments read as current behaviour; a one-line note at the branch, or the cleanup card, would stop the next reader. New finding.

N2 (nit) — `dotted-dimension-unbacked-join-parity.test.ts` drops its positive control that a backed relationship path serves on both live strategies. The removal is right for the raw spelling, but the file no longer shows the served case at all; a declared dimension over the backed path would restore it. The REST envelope pin covers the native face only. New finding.

Each implementing file agrees with the rule it implements; M1 and M2 are about what is published and ruled around the code, not the code's own correctness.
